Hi Sergio —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to gather a short note with our expected workload so we can get a firm price for a dedicated GPU pool and reserved commit. High level — please see the bullet points below and tell us what pool size / commit range you’d recommend and what discounts might be available for a 24-month commitment.

- Org: Atlantic Health, ML Platform team
- Primary use: real-time clinical summarization and triage (low-latency chat + long-context summarization)
- Typical requests/day: 45k (business days), 15k (weekends) => ~1.2M/month average
- Average prompt + response tokens: 1200 tokens (avg prompt 400, gen 800)
- Peak concurrent requests: ~220 concurrent low-latency sessions during morning surge (08:00–11:30 local)
- 95th pct latency SLO: 300ms for short-turn chat (<=256 tokens), 99th pct 800ms for long summaries (<=4k tokens)
- Context length: many calls need 4k context, some up to 8k (rare)
- Expected QPS sustained outside peak: ~85 qps
- Priority: deterministic throughput and fallback plan during maintenance/windows

Also attaching the RFI that includes a security checklist (we’ll ping your security team separately). Can you respond with: recommended GPU pool config (GPU count + type), expected sustained throughput and latency guidance, suggested reserved commit levels (monthly/annual options), and an initial discount tier if we sign 24 months?

Appreciate a concise recommendation we can share with procurement.

Best,
Helen

Hi Helen —

Thanks for the clear workload breakdown — that helps a lot. I’ve pulled in Connor (solutions eng) and Laura (pricing lead). Below is an initial recommendation and a couple of clarifying questions so we can refine the committed pricing.

Initial sizing (conservative, for 99th/95th latency SLOs):
- Recommended GPU type: H100 80GB (quant-ready for T5-style families and larger LLMs that need 4k+ context).
- Recommended pool: 12x H100 80GB (balanced for peak concurrency and batching).
  - Expected throughput: ~160 qps sustained at 4k context with aggressive batching and KV caching for long-form; 95th pct short chat latency ~220–280ms, 99th pct long-summary ~650–800ms based on our benchmarks for similar workloads.
  - Cost baseline: list price estimate in attached pricing workbook (row: H100-12pool).

Reserved commit suggestion (two options):
- Option A (conservative): 12-GPU pool committed for 12 months. ~10% discount off list monthly reserved rate.
- Option B (aggressive): 12-GPU pool committed for 24 months + 20% prepay (annualized) discount: total effective discount ~18–22% depending on prepay cadence and support SLA (priority bursts).

Questions to refine:
1) What percentage of requests are stateful (KV/cache hits) vs cold-starts? If KV hit rate > 40% we can reduce pool size by ~15% via cache savings.
2) How often do you expect 8k-context requests? (even rare 1–2% of traffic can drive footprint).
3) Do you expect regular scheduled nighttime batch jobs that could be colocated on the same pool (we can trade off reserved commit for bursting)?

I’m attaching a pricing workbook with the baseline numbers — Connor, can you add an engineering note on expected token/sec per GPU for their token distribution?

Sergio

Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Quick engineering notes and assumptions used to produce the latency/throughput estimates Sergio shared:

Assumptions from Atlantic payloads:
- Avg tokens/request: 1,200 (400 prompt + 800 gen) -> average sequence length used in perf calc: 1,200
- Peak concurrent sessions: 220 (burst window)
- Token distribution: 70% <512 tokens, 25% between 512–4k, 5% 4k–8k

Performance numbers (H100 80GB) for a mixed BART/OPT-style serving config with quantization and KV caching:
- Single GPU sustained token/sec (mixed distribution, batching enabled): ~45k tokens/sec
- Effective qps per GPU (weighted by token distribution): ~12–14 qps for 1,200 tokens avg
- For 12 GPUs -> theoretical sustained qps ~150–165 qps; with KV caching and request-level prefix caching we reach effective ~170–185 qps in our tests with similar mixes

Sizing rationale: 12 GPUs gives headroom for morning surge + background batch work; if Atlantic can guarantee a KV cache hit rate >= 40% and route low-latency chat to a smaller model variant for 70% of chat traffic we can reduce to 10 GPUs with comparable SLOs (recommendation: 10–12 GPU pool with a performance guardrail).

Burst and fallback options:
- Dedicated + burst pool (extra 2 GPUs on demand) available during morning surge windows for a delta fee; or set policy to fall back to a slightly smaller model (faster quantized variant) if sustained latency starts to slip.

Let us know the cache hit expectation and whether you have any batch jobs to colocate. Happy to run a small synthetic load test next week if you want numbers with Atlantic payloads.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Helen —

Thanks — based on Connor’s numbers and your token distribution notes I’d propose the following commercial path for procurement to review quickly:

1) Recommended contract: 10-GPU H100 pool (H100-10) committed for 24 months with quarterly billing and a 14% committed-use discount + 5% early-signing credit if Atlantic signs within 30 days. This assumes Atlantic will:
   - adopt a light model-variant strategy (route <=70% short chat to a trimmed quantized model),
   - enable KV/prefix caching and target a 40% cache hit rate,
   - avoid colocating heavy nightly batch jobs on the same pool (or schedule them off-peak).

2) Fallback/bursting add-on: 2x H100 burst capacity (on-demand) for morning surge windows at a reduced delta rate (pre-negotiated) so peak concurrency is covered without permanent commit.

3) If Atlantic is unwilling to commit to the operational controls above, maintain a 12-GPU committed footprint — we’ll offer a standard 18% 24-month discount with optional prepay credit tier.

Next steps:
- I’ll update the pricing workbook with Option A (H100-10, 24m, 14% + early sign) and Option B (H100-12, 24m, 18%).
- If procurement wants faster validation, we can schedule a 90-minute load test run next Tue/Thu where we run ~10k synthetic requests/minute for a 20-minute sustained window and capture 95/99 latency.

Would you like me to convert this into a short one-page commercial term sheet for procurement (yes/no)? If yes, I’ll include the burst add-on pricing and cancellation terms.

Best,
Sergio
